title: Signal Triage Sprint Notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick running notes from a focused sprint to tighten alert triage for token/latency regressions. This is a working doc: half playbook, half lab notebook, half scratchpad. Use to run 15–30m investigations and create reproducible bisects or rollback plans.

Context / motivation:
- We keep seeing short-lived latency spikes (50–500ms P95 delta) on prod routes that don't correlate with infra outages. Sometimes these escalate to paging.
- Current investigations take too long because the signal provenance is unclear (is it model, kernel, batch behavior, routing policy, or customer workload?).
- Goal: define a short checklist + a hypothesis matrix and fast commands to get to root cause or a safe rollback path within 30–45 minutes.

How to use this doc:
- Run the Quick Triage checklist below immediately after the alert fires.
- Populate hypothesis matrix with observed facts, update confidence and action.
- If candidate commit/model is found, follow the Bisect & Canary steps.

Quick triage checklist (ordered, <30m):
1) Scope the signal (2–4m)
   - Which route(s) did the alert fire on? (route id from alert payload)
   - Time window: t0 (alert start) -> t1 (alert end or now).
   - Affected region(s)/capacity pool(s) and customer tier.
2) Dashboard snapshot (3–6m)
   - Open Grafana: serving-latency-overview and route-level timeseries. Check P50/P95/P99, cpu/gpu utilization, queue depth.
   - Check KV cache hit ratios and prefix cache activity (route-level panels).
   - Note any step-changes concurrent with t0: model switch, new canary, autoscaler events.
3) Correlate infra events (3–6m)
   - k8s events for pods serving route(s): kubectl get events -n inference --since=10m -o wide
   - Check instance preemption or OOMs: gcloud/azure/az events or internal cloud logs.
   - Check node-level telemetry: host CPU steal, thermal events.
4) Quick profile snapshot (5–10m)
   - If we can reproduce or capture current traffic, run a short flame/profile:
     - curl -H 'x-route: <route>' ... to the debug endpoint that toggles sample-profiling on for 1 minute.
     - Collect /api/debug/profile/<run-id> and upload to flamegraph viewer.
   - If not reproducible, pull last available profiling artifacts from s3: s3://profiling/serving/<route>/<date>/
5) Look for workload changes (2–4m)
   - Query token length distribution for window t0..t1 against baseline (previous 24h):
     - SELECT bucket, count(*) FROM tokens.events WHERE route = '<route>' AND ts BETWEEN '<t0>' AND '<t1>' GROUP BY bucket;
   - Check for sudden rise in long-sequence requests or heavy embedding/attention workloads.
6) Hypothesis quicklist -> action (ongoing)
   - Model change detected -> roll back model alias or switch to compatible variant, create rollback PR.
   - Kernel/hardware pressure -> migrate shards away from affected nodes, schedule rebalance.
   - Autoscaler oscillation -> pin minReplicas temporarily and tune cooldown.
   - Workload burst (long inputs) -> enable short-path quantized model or throttle route.

Hypothesis matrix (columns: hypothesis | evidence | confidence (1–5) | next action | owner)
- Fill out during investigation. Example rows to seed: 
  - Hypothesis: recent quantization profile applied in last deploy
    Evidence: deployment tags, PR #987 mentions q8 + kernel change
    Confidence: 3
    Next action: push quick revert build and run smoke on staging
    Owner: Samir
  - Hypothesis: KV cache warmed incorrectly due to routing change
    Evidence: cache-hit ratio drop from 95% to 20% at t0
    Confidence: 4
    Next action: force cache warm for top prefixes, check routing policy
    Owner: Diego

Bisect & Canary procedure (if you find candidate change):
- When a candidate commit or rollout window looks suspicious, bisect across deployment versions by creating transient canaries:
  1) Identify commit window: commits between t_before (baseline) and t_alert_start.
  2) Create two canaries: one pinned to baseline commit, one pinned to alert commit; route 1% traffic to each for 10m using rollout API.
  3) Collect same traces/metrics (latency histogram, kv cache, batch sizes) and compare.
  4) If canary shows regression, expand to 10% and prepare rollback plan.
- Commands (internal rollout API):
  - rwctl rollout create --route <route> --variant commit:<sha> --weight 1 --timeout 10m
  - rwctl rollout status <rollout-id>

Dashboards and panels to prioritize during triage:
- route-latency-by-model (P50/P95/P99 stacked by model variant)
- batch-size-distribution (tokens per batch; detect sudden shift to tiny batches)
- kv-cache-hit-by-prefix (top 100 prefixes)
- gpu-kernel-queue-depth (kernel exec queue times)
- request-lifetime-trace-sampler (sampled spans to link to trace playback)
- autoscaler-scaling-events (show rapid scale up/down)

Notes on signals that are frequently misattributed:
- Small P95 blips that are actually due to tracing overhead in debug build. Check build tags.
- Apparent model regression where the real culprit is a routing policy that split traffic to a slower region.
- Multitenant noisy neighbor: short-lived spike correlated with a single customer ID.

Data collection checklist (artifacts to snapshot and attach to incident):
- Grafana links for the 10m window before/after alert.
- Profiling artifacts (flamegraphs, cpu/gpu timelines).
- Request sampling traces (link to trace playback id).
- Deployment history and rollout events (kubectl rollout history / internal rollout logs).
- Broker logs showing queueing/backpressure.

Investigation snippets and useful commands (copy/paste):
- Check route history and model alias: rwctl routes get <route> --history --json | jq .
- Pull recent traces for route: rwctl traces list --route <route> --since 15m --limit 50
- Quick profiling toggle (debug-only): curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.redwood.internal/debug/profiler?route=<route>&dur=60
- Compare P95 across two times:
  - SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) FROM metrics.requests WHERE ts BETWEEN '<t0>' AND '<t1>' AND route = '<route>';

Decision matrix for escalation:
- If confidence >=4 that a single deploy/change is root cause -> prepare rollback and schedule canary rollback.
- If confidence 2–3 and infra signals present -> escalate to infra-on-call for deeper node-level forensic.
- If confidence <=1 and signal noisy -> keep sampling, set temporary suppress for alert until next evaluation window.

Open questions / TODOs (sprint backlog):
- Add automatic extraction of top-k contributing spans for each alert (product: trace-playback integration).
- Create a small UI microflow in Console to run 'quick triage' that snapshots panels and runs the profiling toggle automatically.
- Improve samplers to capture 1% of requests for >= 1 hour after an alert for postmortem.
- Paper over false positives from debug builds by embedding build tag in alert payload.

Postmortem template (short):
- What happened (one-liner)
- Impact (routes, customers, duration)
- Root cause (summary)
- Contributing factors (list)
- Detection & response timeline (who did what and when)
- Remediation and follow-ups (owners, due dates)

Scratchpad / recent run log (raw):
- 2025-02-06 09:13 UTC: Pager fired for route /chat/stream P95 +320ms. Grafana: cache hit drop at 09:11.
- 2025-02-06 09:19 UTC: Short profile run captured increased kernel queue time on GPU-3.
- 2025-02-06 09:27 UTC: Deployed rollback to alias v2.1.3 -> p95 returned to baseline.
- Notes: PR #987 introduced eager KV eviction in warm paths. Strong candidate.

If you take one thing away:
- Have a minimal reproducible artifact (trace + profile + short data query) before escalating or rolling back. Often that is enough to convince infra/product owners and avoid cascading changes.

Links / references:
- Incident playbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.local/display/ENG/Serving+Incident+Playbook
- Profiling utilities repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/profiling-tools

-- end of sprint notes --
